```{r}
site <- c("Brisbane", "Melbourne", "Perth", "Sydney", "Broome", "Darwin", "Orange", 
          "Bunbury", "Cairns", "Adelaide", "Gold Coast", "Canberra", "Newcastle", 
          "Wollongong", "Logan City" )
lon <- c(153.03, 144.96, 115.86, 151.21, 122.23, 130.84, 149.10, 115.64, 145.77, 
         138.6, 153.43, 149.13, 151.78, 150.89, 153.12)
lat <- c(-27.47, -37.91, -31.95, -33.87, 17.96, -12.46, -33.28, -33.33, -16.92, 
         -34.93, -28, -35.28, -32.93, -34.42, -27.64)
#Put all of this inforamtion into one list 
samples <- data.frame(site, lon, lat, row.names="site")
# Extract the data from the Rasterstack for all points 
AUcityprecip<- terra::extract(worldclimprecip, samples)
```

```{r}
Aucityprecip2 <- AUcityprecip %>% 
  as_tibble()%>% 
  add_column(Site = site, .before = "Jan")
```

```{r}
Perthprecip <- Aucityprecip2 %>%
  filter(site=="Perth")
```

```{r}
Perthprecip <- Aucityprecip2[3,]
```

```{r}
hist(as.numeric(Perthprecip))
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
#define where you want the breaks in the historgram
userbreak<-c(5,25,45,65,85,105,125,145,165,185)

# remove the ID and site columns
Perthprecip <- Aucityprecip2 %>%
  filter(site=="Perth")

t<-Perthprecip %>%
 dplyr::select(Jan:Dec)

  hist((as.numeric(t)), 
     breaks=userbreak, 
     col="blue", 
     main="Histogram of Perth Precipitation", 
     xlab="Precipitation", 
     ylab="Frequency")
```

```{r}
exactAus<-terra::mask(Ausprecip, Ausoutline)
```

```{r}
#subset using the known location of the raster
hist(exactAus[[3]], col="red", main ="March precipitation")
```
```{r}
exactAus %>%
  tidyterra::select(Mar)%>%
  hist(., col="red", main ="March precipitation")
```
```{r}
ggplot() +
  # function from tidyterra
  geom_spatraster(
    # the raster 
    data = exactAus,
    # the layer within the raster
    aes(fill = Mar)
  )
```
```{r}
exactAusdf <- exactAus %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
# set up the basic histogram
gghist <- ggplot(exactAusdf, 
                 aes(x=Mar)) + 
  geom_histogram(color="black", 
                 fill="white")+
  labs(title="Ggplot2 histogram of Australian March precipitation", 
       x="Precipitation", 
       y="Frequency")
# add a vertical line to the histogram showing mean precipitation
gghist + geom_vline(aes(xintercept=mean(Mar, 
                                        na.rm=TRUE)),
            color="blue", 
            linetype="dashed", 
            size=1)+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```
```{r}
squishdata<-exactAusdf%>%
  pivot_longer(
  cols = 1:12,
  names_to = "Month",
  values_to = "Precipitation"
)
```

```{r}
twomonths <- squishdata %>%
  # | = OR
  filter(., Month=="Jan" | Month=="Jun")
```

```{r}
meantwomonths <- twomonths %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarise(mean=mean(Precipitation, na.rm=TRUE))

meantwomonths
```

```{r}
ggplot(twomonths, aes(x=Precipitation, color=Month, fill=Month)) +
  geom_histogram(position="identity", alpha=0.5)+
  geom_vline(data=meantwomonths, 
             aes(xintercept=mean, 
                 color=Month),
             linetype="dashed")+
  labs(title="Ggplot2 histogram of Australian Jan and Jun
       precipitation",
       x="Precipitation",
       y="Frequency")+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```
```{r}
data_complete_cases <- squishdata %>%
  drop_na()%>% 
  mutate(Month = factor(Month, levels = c("Jan","Feb","Mar",
                                          "Apr","May","Jun",
                                          "Jul","Aug","Sep",
                                          "Oct","Nov","Dec")))

# Plot faceted histogram
ggplot(data_complete_cases, aes(x=Precipitation, na.rm=TRUE))+
  geom_histogram(color="black", binwidth = 5)+
  labs(title="Ggplot2 faceted histogram of Australian precipitation", 
       x="Precipitation",
       y="Frequency")+
  facet_grid(Month ~ .)+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```
```{r}
install.packages("plotly")
```


```{r}
library(plotly)
# split the data for plotly based on month

jan <- squishdata %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  filter(., Month=="Jan")

jun <- squishdata %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  filter(., Month=="Jun")

# give axis titles
x <- list (title = "Precipitation")
y <- list (title = "Frequency")

# set the bin width
xbinsno<-list(start=0, end=40, size = 2.5)

# plot the histogram calling all the variables we just set
ihist<-plot_ly(alpha = 0.6) %>%
        add_histogram(x = jan$Precipitation,
        xbins=xbinsno, name="January") %>%
        add_histogram(x = jun$Precipitation,
        xbins=xbinsno, name="June") %>% 
        layout(barmode = "overlay", xaxis=x, yaxis=y)

ihist
```

```{r}
# mean per month
meanofall <- squishdata %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(Precipitation, na.rm=TRUE))

# print the top 1
head(meanofall, n=1)
```

```{r}
# standard deviation per month
sdofall <- squishdata %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarize(sd = sd(Precipitation, na.rm=TRUE))

# maximum per month
maxofall <- squishdata %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarize(max = max(Precipitation, na.rm=TRUE))

# minimum per month
minofall <- squishdata %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarize(min = min(Precipitation, na.rm=TRUE))

# Interquartlie range per month
IQRofall <- squishdata %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarize(IQR = IQR(Precipitation, na.rm=TRUE))

# perhaps you want to store multiple outputs in one list..
lotsofstats <- squishdata %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarize(IQR = IQR(Precipitation, na.rm=TRUE), 
            max=max(Precipitation, na.rm=T))

# or you want to know the mean (or some other stat) 
#for the whole year as opposed to each month...

meanwholeyear=squishdata %>%
  summarize(meanyear = mean(Precipitation, na.rm=TRUE))
```
